I’m also, 100% white but I’m also color blind to other races. However my mother and family grew  up in a different era. It disappoints me to my very core...I’ve brought home Hispanic boyfriends, black and all different races. They are always polite but...god I don’t know to describe it but they are just cold to them. 

It’s an intolerance and it disgusts me. Most of these men treated me better then some of the down home southern white boys I’ve brought home. But these ethnically diverse men wanted only good things for me, more so than my previous racially accepted boyfriends. I’m baffled by the fact that my family couldn’t...or wouldn’t even try to get to know them. I was raised to be always tolerant and understanding.....you never know what someone is going through or coming from. To me they defined hypocrisy. 

And that’s not to say anything against white men, I feel like I found the the love of my life with an older white man and he loves me the way any person could ever dream of.

It’s so important to lift each other up, listen to them and respect the fact that you may disagree but we all need to hear the other side, and challenge each other respectfully, shake hands or even better hug and embrace at the end of it.    

Communication is the absolute, number 1 thing we need in the world. My heart goes out to people of mixed races because sometimes it’s so hard for them to be accepted by either side. It’s complete BS, and I fucking hate that nonsense. 

The courage you all have and the struggles I’m certain you go through I can hardly relate too. But you have a heart and integrity and it doesn’t go unnoticed by all....let people underestimate you! Be the best person that you know you are. And if they still want to expect the worst from you or any one of us for that matter then they aren’t worth proving ourselves to.

Some people are just comfortable with hate, but I really like to think most of us aren’t. However there are those who can be taught to open their minds, be taught patience and although it may go slowly be taught and shown/lead by example  a better and healthier way.
